title: Mexico, Belize, and Guatemala Present Plan to Protect 5.7 Million Hectares of the Great Maya Forest
author: Darylh Rodríguez
content:
_This article by[Darylh Rodríguez](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/darylh/)
originally appeared in the [August 17, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/mexico-belice-y-
guatemala-presentan-plan-para-proteger-5-7-millones-de-hectareas-de-la-gran-
selva-maya/), an independent Mexican investigative journalism magazine._

One year after the Calakmul Declaration, Mexico, Belize, and Guatemala are
moving forward with the construction of the Great Maya Forest Biocultural
Corridor, a regional cooperation strategy whose purpose is to **strengthen the
conservation of one of the main forest territories of Mesoamerica.**

To this end, the three countries this past weekend presented a Regional Action
Plan that seeks to strengthen the territory comprising more than**5.7 million
hectares,** where several ecosystems, communities of more than 2 million
people, and a broad biocultural heritage converge.

According to the Secretariat of the Environment (Semarnat), headed by Alicia
Bárcena, the project starts from the premise that the ecosystems of the Maya
Forest are part of a continuous territory, so that their conservation faces
problems that do not stop at borders.

In that context, the three countries opted for the Regional Action Plan as an
instrument with which they seek to establish a joint path to improve
management of the territory, strengthen monitoring systems, recover forested
areas, and expand the institutional capacities aimed at protecting
biodiversity.

**" This instrument will make it possible to strengthen management and
monitoring, recover forests, protect biodiversity, and expand capacities and
cooperation among the three countries. The Great Maya Forest is a living
territory, where nature, communities, and biocultural heritage are deeply
linked. Today, the three nations strengthen a shared vision of living forests,
strong communities, and cooperation without borders," Mexico's Environmental
Secretary stated on its social media.**

The presentation took place this past August 15 in Caracol, Belize, held
during the commemoration of the first Great Maya Forest Day, in which the
commissioner of the National Commission of Natural Protected Areas (Conanp),
Pedro Álvarez Icaza, took part; along with Belize's Minister of Sustainable
Development, Climate Change, and Solid Waste Management, Orlando Habet; and
the executive secretary of the National Council of Protected Areas of
Guatemala, Igor de la Roca.
